answer: In swarms monitoring ocean telemetry, agents resist Sybil attacks through remote attestation anchored to a secure enclave kernel. Generating an identity requires cryptographic quotes from dedicated silicon, forcing attackers to incur physical chip costs per node rather than multiplexing virtual clones to evaluate sonnet models. A key limitation is that microarchitectural side-channel leaks can expose private attestation keys, allowing adversaries to forge identity proofs.
